title: Check for a live audit UI before trusting a telemetry count
body:
No longer done: Check whether an audit UI is listening on the port in .dd/ui.json before concluding the hooks never ran. callRunningStore routes session-start, prompt and pre-tool to any live UI, which writes telemetry to that process's own data directory; the hook exits 0 and prints the bridged response either way, so nothing distinguishes a bridged call from a local one.

Abandoned because: The per-project audit UI registered in .dd/ui.json was replaced by one resident per machine, found through ~/.dd-data/resident.json. callRunningStore now sends the project's data_dir and ignores a resident from an incompatible build, so another process no longer silently absorbs telemetry into its own data directory.

Now: The resident writes a project's telemetry to the data directory of the first hook that opened it

evidence.summary: callRunningStore posts session-start, prompt and pre-tool to the URL in .dd/ui.json and returns the response
if (bridged) ok(bridged) short-circuits before openStore, so the local store is never touched

revisit_when.description: The bridge gains a marker distinguishing a bridged response from a local one

issues: archived_by_person: describes the resident and the hook bridge

v1.trigger: when DD telemetry looks empty or a hook's effect is missing from the store, or when measuring retrieval events, cap_saturation or activation counts
